thread_analysis.thread_summary: Nippon Seiki Co., Ltd. (contact Kohei Yonehara, EMS Design) maintains a multi-year relationship (December 2022 through March 2025) with Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Jun Wang, Yuka Nakamura) for Bluetooth SIG certification of a 'Holfee' sensor/gateway product line, spanning initial RF PHY testing and registration through numerous subsequent derivative-model hardware revisions (buzzer circuit and connector changes, PCB/enclosure size changes, additional sensor circuitry in alternate board layouts) and a Model Number reuse question, plus standard onboarding logistics (required documents, sample submission scope, test duration, payment terms) and registration-site navigation updates following the 2024 Qualification Workspace migration.
all_questions_found: Does each of several hardware revisions (buzzer circuit/connector, PCB/enclosure size, added sensor circuitry) still qualify as a free derivative model without retest? (see thread_0274_case_01)
Does reusing a Model Number across design revisions create a registration conflict or compliance gap? (see thread_0274_case_02)

(Administrative, initial onboarding FAQ) What documents are needed for the initial application, is PCB ASSY alone sufficient for the test sample, how long does RF PHY testing (mandatory + 2M + Coded, 27 items) take, and what are the payment terms?

(Administrative) Where can already-registered products be viewed on the new Qualification Workspace site, and how has the derivative-model registration procedure changed since the 2024 site migration?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The core recurring technical principle across this multi-year relationship is that Bluetooth certification's free derivative-model eligibility depends solely on the BLE-relevant signal path (chip firmware and antenna-feed circuit/routing) remaining unchanged, independent of any other hardware modification — a narrower, more permissive standard than Japan's Radio Law technical conformity certification's broader re-application trigger (any board shape or appearance change). Separately, Model Number reuse across design revisions doesn't create a registration conflict, since SIG compliance hinges on the labeled Model Number being searchable in the registration database, not on the Product List visually distinguishing design revisions.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0274_case_01 and thread_0274_case_02 for the specific decision logic; the administrative/onboarding content follows standard patterns already documented in other threads (required Compliance Folder documents, sample submission scope, lab routing for RF PHY test items beyond the mandatory set).
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See thread_0274_case_01 and thread_0274_case_02 for specific risks.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified — Allion consistently and correctly applied the same narrow derivative-model criterion across many years and many distinct hardware change proposals, and proactively flagged the separate, stricter Japan Radio Law re-application trigger to prevent the customer from conflating the two regimes.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For long-term customers with an evolving product line built on a stable Bluetooth registration, consistently apply the same narrow BLE-signal-path-unchanged criterion for free derivative-model eligibility across every new hardware revision proposal, and proactively distinguish this permissive Bluetooth standard from other certifications (like Japan's Radio Law) that have broader, stricter re-application triggers the customer must track separately.
